subject: SummitBridge renewal: usage health & pricing pathway
messages:
From: Arielle Kline <arielle.k@summitbridge.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwoodai.com
Cc: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.kumar@summitbridge.ai>, procurement@summitbridge.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Mar 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning - usage trend questions

Hi Mateo,

We're starting the internal review ahead of our May renewal and I wanted to pull a couple of threads with you before we loop procurement. High level: our token spend in Q1 shifted noticeably toward embeddings (≈48% of tokens) after the search migration, and we have a few latency-sensitive user journeys that are now exposed in production.

Can you confirm:
- whether the hosted plan we're on supports reserved burst capacity for embeddings-heavy days, and
- whether you can share a short ROI summary comparing keeping hosted vs committing to a 12-month Dedicated pool (ballpark numbers are fine).

Also tagging Rajesh for ops context — our 95th-percentile latency target for the user flow is 220ms. We saw a few spikes above 400ms during last month's campaign.

Thanks,
Arielle
Head of Product, SummitBridge

Attachments: none

From: mateo_alvarez@redwoodai.com
To: Arielle Kline <arielle.k@summitbridge.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com, jasmine_liu@redwoodai.com
Date: Wed, 29 Mar 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning - usage trend questions

Arielle — thanks for the heads-up. Quick notes and suggested next steps.

Short answers:
- Hosted (current) supports burst lanes but they're subject to regional availability and can't guarantee a long-running latency SLO at the committed throughput level you described.
- We can build a straight-line ROI comparison for Hosted vs 12-month Dedicated; I've attached a raw usage export (Q1) and a latency SLO summary to start.

Preliminary observations from your Q1 export:
- Avg daily tokens: 38M; peak day: 85M (embeddings-heavy).
- Token split: embeddings 48%, chat/generation 36%, reranking/other 16%.
- Latency spikes correlate with high-concurrency batches to the embeddings endpoint.

Recommendation (high level):
1) Short pilot (4–6 weeks) on a small Dedicated pool sized for your 95th-percentile concurrency (reduces p95 latency by ~35–45% in our benchmarks for similar workloads).
2) If pilot meets latency and cost targets, convert to a 12-month commit with a stepped capacity plan (start smaller, auto-scale at 60% utilization).

I'll loop Karthik for pricing/terms and Jasmine for the pilot ops checklist. Proposed meeting slots: Thu 4/4 10:00 or Mon 4/8 14:00 PT.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: summitbridge-usage-2028Q1.csv (csv), latency-slo-summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.kumar@summitbridge.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwoodai.com
Cc: Arielle Kline <arielle.k@summitbridge.ai>, procurement@summitbridge.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Apr 2028 11:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning - usage trend questions

Thanks Mateo — got the files, and the numbers look sensible. A couple of clarifying points from our side before the pilot: 

1) Cost sensitivity: our finance lead won't sign off on a 12-month commit unless the expected unit cost improvement is at least 20% vs hosted over the year (accounting for expected 30% growth).
2) Data residency: we need the Dedicated pool to be in us-west-2.
3) Operational ask: can you guarantee a runbook for failover to hosted if Dedicated capacity becomes constrained during a black-swan event?

We can take the 4/8 14:00 PT meeting — Arielle and I will be there, procurement may join depending on outcome.

- Rajesh
VP Engineering, SummitBridge

> Arielle — thanks for the heads-up. Quick notes and suggested next steps.
> [attached usage CSV and latency summary]

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com
To: Arielle Kline <arielle.k@summitbridge.ai>, Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.kumar@summitbridge.ai>, mateo_alvarez@redwoodai.com
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwoodai.com
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning - usage trend questions

Arielle/Rajesh — great sync yesterday, appreciate the candid constraints. Follow-up with the ROI recap and a pilot + term recommendation below.

ROI recap (yearly view, ballpark):
- Baseline (Hosted, extrapolated 30% growth): $1,200,000
- Dedicated 12-month (start 40% of peak capacity, autoscale ladders): $920,000
- Net savings: ~$280,000 (~23% lower than baseline)
- Key drivers: 1) better GPU utilization on embeddings (quantized kernels + batching) 2) lower per-token egress on internal caching layer 3) lower preemption/overhead vs burst-hosted lanes

Pilot proposal (4 weeks):
- Size: Dedicated pool configured in us-west-2 sized for 60% of observed peak concurrency (should reduce p95 latency to target ~200ms).
- Success criteria: p95 latency <= 220ms for two rolling weeks AND effective unit cost reduction >= 15% in pilot window (we model full-year uplift separately).
- Failover: We'll provide an automated routing policy that can reroute to hosted in a capacity event; there is a documented runbook (we'll share) and an optional SLA credit if we miss scheduled failover tests.

Commercials / Terms (starter):
- Pilot: free pilot credits for first 4 weeks (infra cost covered by Redwood).
- 12-month commit: if you convert within 30 days after pilot, we can offer a stepped discount schedule up to 12% off list pricing and a one-time onboarding credit equal to one month of committed capacity.
- If you need a deeper discount to hit +20% overall savings vs Hosted, we can model a 24-month cadence or larger initial commit.

Next steps:
1) Confirm pilot start window (we suggested 4/15).
2) We will send a short pilot checklist and the draft amendment (attached).
3) Procurement and your finance team to share any mandatory contract terms we should pre-clear.

I'll attach the draft amendment and the pilot checklist to the HubSpot deal record after this. Mateo will own scheduling and ops kickoff.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft-amendment-12mo.docx (docx)
